goal: Produce a proved native Lean repository whose immutable public boundary exports FinitePairwiseCoverageGap.finite_pairwise_coverage_gap. The result must retain monotonicity, submodularity, unrestricted optimum 4, nonempty pairwise-feasible distributions, the universal pairwise upper bound 479/160, and the strict ratio comparison, over the complete real-valued feasible domain.

interface_inputs.expected_statement_lean_code:
theorem finite_pairwise_coverage_gap :
    (∀ ⦃s t : Finset Element⦄, s ⊆ t → coverage s ≤ coverage t) ∧
    (∀ s t : Finset Element,
      coverage (s ∪ t) + coverage (s ∩ t) ≤ coverage s + coverage t) ∧
    IsUnrestrictedOptimum 4 ∧
    IsPairwiseUpperBound (479 / 160) ∧
    (4 : ℝ) / (479 / 160) > 4 / 3 := by
  sorry
interface_inputs.name: FinitePairwiseCoverageGap.finite_pairwise_coverage_gap
interface_inputs.note: The public theorem must keep the universal real distribution quantifiers. Do not replace the paper-faithful upper bound by the survey-only 15-atom equality extension.
interface_inputs.summary: A five-element monotone submodular coverage function has unrestricted value 4 while every pairwise-independent feasible distribution has value at most 479/160, giving a ratio above 4/3.

notes: Use the complete 32-row exact dual certificate from the SourceCorpus. Weak duality and all finite probability algebra belong in this native repository; no external provider repository is planned.
source_description: Faithful mathematical extraction of Ramachandra and Natarajan's finite coverage counterexample, including all exact primal and dual certificates and a single Lean target.
